quarterly_data.quarter: Hygon Information Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual collective (04-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Director and general manager Sha Chaoqun (2025 annual collective results briefing) on DCU generations: Shensuan-3 (Deep Computing No. 3) DCU reached commercial use in 2025 and has been deployed in research, healthcare, astronomy and other fields, covering AI training and inference, scientific computing and financial risk control; R&D of the next-generation Shensuan-4 is progressing smoothly, under a 'sell one generation, validate one, develop one' strategy. He said Hygon's DCU is one of the few domestic GPGPU chips that support both full-precision and half-precision AI training and inference, and the DCU line is tiered by customer scenario between high-end training compute and low-latency, high-efficiency inference products, with its DTK software stack fully opened.

quarterly_data.quarter: Hygon Information Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual collective (04-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: General manager Sha Chaoqun (2025 annual collective results briefing): with 2025 revenue up 56.92%, the top five customers' share of sales fell from 98.16% to 90.28%, which he called an improvement in customer concentration reflecting a more diversified customer base. He said the DCU had been fully adapted and jointly tuned with 365 mainstream large models, covering 99% of the world's non-closed-source large models, and that the ecosystem's common gaps at this stage are deep tuning of very large clusters, operator optimisation and integrated vertical-industry solutions. He also said the company will keep R&D investment at a high intensity long term.
quarterly_data.figure: top five customers 90.28% of 2025 sales (from 98.16%); 365 models, 99% of non-closed-source large models

quarterly_data.quarter: Hygon Information Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual collective (04-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: General manager Sha Chaoqun's view (2025 annual collective results briefing): as AI agents and AI inference grow, task scheduling, reasoning and multi-service coordination sharply raise demand for general-purpose computing and for CPU concurrency and memory capacity, and Hygon's CPUs are expected to raise their penetration of the commercial market; over the next three to five years competition among intelligent computing centers will shift from build-out scale to energy efficiency, cluster utilisation and full-lifecycle cost, which Hygon is addressing by optimising CPU and DCU architectures and strengthening high-speed interconnect and super-node technology.
